ИТОГОВЫЙ ОТВЕТ

■ Естественный ответ (для полей answer/payload.hypothesis)

EN: "In all three observed years — 1985, 1990 and 1996 — respondents with a criminal record (ever_jailed = 1, i.e. jailed between 1985 and 1994; n = 289) held significantly lower composite wealth than those never jailed (n = 11,724), and the gap widened over time. In 1985 mean wealth was $7,929 vs $25,086 (difference −$17,157; 95% CI −20,603 to −13,711; bootstrap −20,364 to −13,621; one-sided Welch p = 3.2e-21, Holm p = 9.5e-21; Mann–Whitney p = 8.0e-11; Cliff's δ = −0.22; medians $720 vs $3,600); in 1990, $16,350 vs $73,948 (−$57,598; CI −69,428 to −45,768; p = 7.8e-20, Holm 7.8e-20; MWU 3.9e-35; δ = −0.42; medians $0 vs $10,500); in 1996, $20,383 vs $105,447 (−$85,063; CI −102,274 to −67,853; p = 3.6e-20, Holm 7.3e-20; MWU 4.6e-26; δ = −0.35; medians $0 vs $8,500). The pattern survives adjustment for sex and race (asinh-wealth β = −0.49, −1.45, −1.63; all p ≤ 1.7e-06), median regression (−$1,100, −$3,800, −$6,000), permutation tests and all sensitivity variants; the wealth ratio fell 0.32 → 0.22 → 0.19. This is descriptive/associational, not causal: the exposure window is 1985–1994, so the 1985 difference reflects a pre-existing wealth gap / selection into incarceration rather than a consequence of it; the data are unweighted and contain 1,899 exact duplicate rows, so they are not representative of the U.S. population."

Поправки на пол/расу, медианная регрессия, permutation и все варианты чувствительности направление подтверждают. Формулировка ассоциативная: окно экспозиции 1985–1994, поэтому разрыв 1985 — предшествующее различие/селекция; данные невзвешены и содержат 1 899 точных дубликатов.»

■ Пределы (уже включены в гипотезу): «судимость» = только лишение свободы 1985–1994 (столбцов места жительства нет, косвенная мера не строилась); весов нет; 1 899 точных дубликатов; нули могут включать nonresponse (в 1996 — 38% нулей); нет ID/возраста/дохода, поэтому скорректировать отток и совариаты кроме пола и расы нельзя.

payload.hypothesis: In all three observed years - 1985, 1990 and 1996 - respondents with a criminal record (ever_jailed = 1, jailed between 1985 and 1994; n = 289) held significantly lower composite wealth than those never jailed (n = 11,724), and the gap widened over time. In 1985 mean wealth was $7,929 vs $25,086 (difference -$17,157; 95% CI -20,603 to -13,711; bootstrap -20,364 to -13,621; one-sided Welch p = 3.2e-21, Holm-adjusted 9.5e-21; Mann-Whitney p = 8.0e-11; Cliff's delta = -0.22; medians $720 vs $3,600); in 1990 $16,350 vs $73,948 (-$57,598; CI -69,428 to -45,768; p = 7.8e-20, Holm 7.8e-20; MWU 3.9e-35; delta = -0.42; medians $0 vs $10,500); in 1996 $20,383 vs $105,447 (-$85,063; CI -102,274 to -67,853; p = 3.6e-20, Holm 7.3e-20; MWU 4.6e-26; delta = -0.35; medians $0 vs $8,500). The pattern survives adjustment for sex and race (asinh-wealth beta = -0.49, -1.45, -1.63; all p <= 1.7e-06), median regression (-$1,100, -$3,800, -$6,000), permutation tests, and every sensitivity variant (zeros treated as missing, wealth>0 only, deduplicated rows, winsorized, trimmed means); the wealth ratio fell from 0.32 to 0.22 to 0.19, and both the share with wealth <= 0 (45/57/63% vs 32/29/40%) and mean wealth among positive-wealth respondents (difference -$22k, -$67k, -$121k) contributed. The association is descriptive, not causal: the exposure window is 1985-1994, so the 1985 difference reflects a pre-existing wealth gap / selection into incarceration rather than a consequence of it, and the unweighted data (1,899 exact duplicate rows; wealth zeros that may include survey nonresponse) are not representative of the U.S. population.
payload.workflow: 1) QC of data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 x 6, no missing values, race label 'hipanic' kept, ever_jailed 289 vs 11,724, 1,899 exact duplicate rows noted). 2) Main sample = full file; exposure = ever_jailed only, no derived features. 3) Primary per-year contrasts on raw dollars (1985, 1990, 1996): one-sided Welch t-test (H1: jailed < never) and one-sided Mann-Whitney U, with Holm correction across the 3 years within each test family at alpha = 0.05; two-sided p-values and 95% t CIs reported alongside; 10,000-replicate percentile bootstrap CIs for differences in means and medians; 10,000-swap permutation test as a distribution-free check. 4) Effect sizes: Cliff's delta on raw wealth, Hedges g on asinh(wealth/1000). 5) Confirmatory regressions: OLS asinh(wealth/1000) ~ ever_jailed + C(sex) + C(race) with HC3 SEs (unadjusted coefficient shown in the same table) and median (quantile) regression with the same covariates. 6) Decision rule: a year counts as robust if direction agrees in all analyses (mean difference, median difference, adjusted asinh beta, median-regression beta, Cliff's delta) AND Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 in both primary families. 7) Decomposition of the gap into the extensive margin (share with wealth <= 0; chi-square and logistic regression adjusted for sex+race) and the intensive margin E[wealth | wealth > 0] with bootstrap CI, showing the finding is not produced by zero-filled attrition. 8) Sensitivity: A main (zeros+duplicates kept), B zeros as missing, C wealth>0 only, D exact duplicate rows dropped, E winsorized at 1st/99th percentile, plus Yuen-Welch 10%-trimmed means. 9) Exploratory sex x race appendix with cell sizes (n_jailed 9-16 in female cells) flagged as low power and excluded from the answer wording. 10) Outputs: results_table_primary.csv, results_table_sensitivity.csv, results_table_appendix_sexrace.csv, results_summary.md.
payload.sensitivity_summary: 15/15 variant x year cells show a negative difference and Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 (A main, B zeros-as-missing, C wealth>0, D dedup, E winsorized); Yuen-Welch 10%-trimmed p = 1.1e-31 (1985), 9.9e-215 (1990), 3.5e-186 (1996). Conclusion independent of zero handling and duplicate handling.
limitations: criminal record operationalised only as jail 1985-1994; no other record type available in the file
associational, not causal; 1985 precedes most of the exposure window
no survey weights -> not population representative
1,899 exact duplicate rows retained in the main run
wealth zeros may include survey nonresponse/attrition; no participation flag, ID, age or income to adjust for selection beyond sex and race
sex x race cells have 9-16 exposed cases (exploratory only, low power)
